hints: Focus on the type of reaction occurring when an alcohol is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid: dehydration to yield an alkene.
Notice that secondary and tertiary ring alcohols can eliminate a hydrogen atom from more than one adjacent ring carbon, forming multiple alkene isomers.
Look for the primary alcohol where the adjacent ring carbon has only one hydrogen atom available for elimination, giving a unique alkene product.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Heating an alcohol with an excess of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes acid-catalysed dehydration (elimination of water) to produce an alkene:

$$\text{alcohol} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{alkene} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Analyze dehydration pathways for options A, B, and C**

In compounds A, B, and C, the $-\text{OH}$ group is attached directly to the six-membered ring (secondary or tertiary alcohols). Elimination of water can remove a proton from either of the two adjacent ring carbon atoms, creating a mixture of position isomers or stereoisomers (such as 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene and 2,3-dimethylcyclohexene).

**Examine option D and conclude**

In D, the alcohol is (2-methylcyclohexyl)methanol, a primary alcohol with the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group attached to carbon-1 of the ring. Elimination removes $-\text{OH}$ and the single hydrogen on C1 to form an exocyclic double bond $(=\text{CH}_2)$. Because there is only one hydrogen on C1 and a terminal $=\text{CH}_2$ group has no cis-trans isomers, exactly one organic product is formed.

options.A: Incorrect. In 3,4-dimethylcyclohexanol, the secondary -OH group can eliminate with a hydrogen from either adjacent ring carbon (C2 or C4), producing a mixture of isomeric alkenes rather than a single organic product.
options.B: Incorrect. In 2,3-dimethylcyclohexanol, elimination of water can occur toward C2 or toward C6, giving a mixture of different alkene structural isomers.
options.C: Incorrect. In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexanol, dehydration of the tertiary alcohol can remove a hydrogen from C2 (giving 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene), from C6, or from the C1 methyl group, producing multiple alkene products.
options.D: Correct. In (2-methylcyclohexyl)methanol, the primary -CH2OH group dehydrates by losing -OH and the single hydrogen on the adjacent ring carbon C1. This yields exclusively 1-methyl-2-methylenecyclohexane with an exocyclic double bond, forming only one organic product.
